card: Bitcoin Core currently uses all-zero auxiliary data when creating Schnorr signatures for Taproot inputs, omitting BIP340-recommended defense-in-depth protections against fault-injection and side-channel attacks. This PR changes MutableTransactionSignatureCreator to supply fresh randomness via GetRandHash() by default, while introducing an aux_rand field in SignOptions to permit fixed auxiliary values when needed. It updates BIP341 keypath unit tests to verify both vector reproducibility with zero aux_rand and signature divergence under default options, and seeds the RNG in the script_sign fuzz target. Resolves issue #31883.
changed_since_previous: Added SignOptions::aux_rand to allow callers to explicitly pass fixed auxiliary data instead of always forcing fresh randomness, enabling the BIP341 keypath test vector to continue verifying exact signature bytes alongside a test that consecutive default signatures differ.
evidence: BIP340 specification explicitly recommends fresh randomness as auxiliary data for side-channel and fault-injection mitigation (cited in PR description and commit 1f274eae23).
Linked issue #31883: 'SignatureCreator should supply auxiliary data argument for additional bip340 signature security'.
problem: Bitcoin Core signs Taproot inputs with all-zero auxiliary data instead of fresh randomness. This foregoes the defense-in-depth protection against side-channel and fault-injection attacks recommended by BIP340.

risk.why: A flaw in signature creation or RNG handling could produce invalid transaction signatures or degrade Schnorr signing robustness for wallet users.

scope_notes: Small patch touching transaction signing helper logic and tests.
summary: Passes fresh randomness from GetRandHash() as BIP340 auxiliary data when creating Schnorr signatures in MutableTransactionSignatureCreator, replacing the static all-zero value. Adds a SignOptions::aux_rand option so callers can supply a fixed auxiliary value when deterministic signatures are required. Updates the BIP341 keypath unit test to test both fixed and randomized signing, and seeds the RNG in the script_sign fuzz target.
